title: Number of Submatrices That Sum to Target
description:
Given an `m x n` integer `matrix` and an integer `target`, return the number of non-empty rectangular submatrices whose elements sum to `target`.

A submatrix `(r1, c1, r2, c2)` consists of all cells `(r, c)` with `r1 <= r <= r2` and `c1 <= c <= c2`. Two submatrices are distinct if they differ in any boundary coordinate.
hints: Fix the top row r1 and bottom row r2 (or left/right columns if n < m), compressing each column into a single 1D sum.
On the resulting 1D array, count subarrays summing to target in O(n) using a running prefix sum and a frequency hash map initialized with {0: 1}.

examples.explanation: Four 1x1 submatrices contain 0: the four corners of the 3x3 matrix.
Five submatrices sum to 0: two 1x1 cells, two 1x2/2x1 pairs, and the entire 2x2 matrix.
The single cell [904] does not equal target 0, so the count is 0.
